# Check catalogue

Every check the audit runs. All of them are deterministic: no model is
involved, so a given page always produces the same findings and an
audit costs nothing to produce.

**74 checks** across 12 categories.

## Prioritisation

Findings are ranked by `impact x confidence / effort`, scaled by how
many pages they affect. The inputs are in the table so the ranking can
be argued with rather than taken on faith.

**Fix** means the platform can apply the change itself when autonomy
allows. Everything else needs a person or a developer.

## aeo

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `content_needs_javascript` | critical | The page's content only exists after JavaScript runs | 0.90 | 0.70 | - |
| `ai_crawler_blocked` | high | AI crawlers are blocked | 0.70 | 0.20 | auto |
| `meta_needs_javascript` | high | Title or description is injected by script rather than served | 0.70 | 0.40 | - |
| `seo_injection_script` | high | An SEO tool is injecting fixes client side | 0.60 | 0.50 | - |
| `entity_unclear` | medium | The brand entity is not defined | 0.40 | 0.30 | auto |
| `no_author_attribution` | medium | No identifiable author | 0.45 | 0.40 | - |
| `no_citable_facts` | medium | No citable facts or data | 0.45 | 0.60 | - |
| `no_direct_answer` | medium | Page does not answer its question directly | 0.50 | 0.40 | auto |
| `missing_llms_txt` | low | No llms.txt | 0.20 | 0.20 | auto |

**`content_needs_javascript`** — The page's content only exists after JavaScript runs

- *Why it matters:* AI crawlers do not execute JavaScript, so a page whose copy is assembled in the browser is a blank page to every answer engine except Google's.
- *What to do:* Server-render the content, pre-render it at build time, or ship the copy in the initial HTML.

**`ai_crawler_blocked`** — AI crawlers are blocked

- *Why it matters:* Blocking GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and friends removes the site from AI answers.
- *What to do:* Decide deliberately: allow the crawlers you want citations from.

**`meta_needs_javascript`** — Title or description is injected by script rather than served

- *Why it matters:* A title set by JavaScript is a title half the machines reading the page never see.
- *What to do:* Put the title and meta description in the HTML the server sends.

**`seo_injection_script`** — An SEO tool is injecting fixes client side

- *Why it matters:* Scripts that apply SEO changes in the browser produce fixes no AI crawler can see, and the changes disappear the day the subscription stops.
- *What to do:* Move those changes into the CMS so they are served in the HTML and survive the tool that suggested them.

**`entity_unclear`** — The brand entity is not defined

- *Why it matters:* Answer engines resolve brands through consistent entity signals, not prose.
- *What to do:* Add Organization schema with sameAs links to the profiles that describe you.

**`no_author_attribution`** — No identifiable author

- *Why it matters:* Experience and expertise cannot be assessed without a real, credentialed author.
- *What to do:* Attribute the page to a named author with a linked bio and credentials.

**`no_citable_facts`** — No citable facts or data

- *Why it matters:* Models cite pages that contain specific numbers, dates and named sources.
- *What to do:* Add original data, specific figures and sourced statements.

**`no_direct_answer`** — Page does not answer its question directly

- *Why it matters:* Answer engines quote the passage that states the answer plainly near the top.
- *What to do:* Open with a two to three sentence direct answer before the detail.

**`missing_llms_txt`** — No llms.txt

- *Why it matters:* An llms.txt gives answer engines a curated map of what matters on the site.
- *What to do:* Publish /llms.txt listing the canonical pages and what each covers.

## analytics

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `analytics_missing` | high | No analytics tag detected | 0.60 | 0.20 | - |
| `gsc_not_connected` | high | Search Console is not connected | 0.80 | 0.10 | - |
| `conversion_tracking_missing` | medium | No conversion tracking | 0.50 | 0.40 | - |

**`analytics_missing`** — No analytics tag detected

- *Why it matters:* Without measurement, nothing that follows can be attributed or defended.
- *What to do:* Install GA4 or your analytics of choice and verify it fires.

**`gsc_not_connected`** — Search Console is not connected

- *Why it matters:* Search Console is the only first-party source of query and indexing truth.
- *What to do:* Connect the property so the platform can work from real data.

**`conversion_tracking_missing`** — No conversion tracking

- *Why it matters:* Ranking without conversion data optimises for the wrong thing.
- *What to do:* Define and instrument the actions that represent revenue.

## compliance

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unsubstantiated_claim` | high | Claim published without substantiation | 0.50 | 0.20 | - |
| `ymyl_no_credentials` | high | Health, legal or financial content with no stated credentials | 0.70 | 0.40 | - |
| `ai_content_unreviewed` | medium | Generated content published without human review | 0.60 | 0.20 | - |
| `missing_disclosure` | medium | Affiliate or sponsored content without disclosure | 0.50 | 0.10 | auto |

**`unsubstantiated_claim`** — Claim published without substantiation

- *Why it matters:* Unsupported superlatives and performance claims carry regulatory risk in most markets.
- *What to do:* Cite the source, soften the claim, or remove it.

**`ymyl_no_credentials`** — Health, legal or financial content with no stated credentials

- *Why it matters:* For topics that affect health or money, unqualified advice is both a ranking and a liability problem.
- *What to do:* Attribute the content to a qualified reviewer and state the credential.

**`ai_content_unreviewed`** — Generated content published without human review

- *Why it matters:* Scaled content produced without oversight is exactly what spam policies target.
- *What to do:* Route through review and add a named human reviewer.

**`missing_disclosure`** — Affiliate or sponsored content without disclosure

- *Why it matters:* Undisclosed commercial relationships breach platform policy and advertising law.
- *What to do:* Add a clear disclosure above the fold.

## content

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `duplicate_content` | high | Duplicate page content | 0.60 | 0.50 | - |
| `thin_content` | high | Thin content | 0.60 | 0.70 | - |
| `title_missing` | high | Missing title tag | 0.80 | 0.10 | auto |
| `content_stale` | medium | Content has not been updated in over 18 months | 0.45 | 0.50 | - |
| `duplicate_title` | medium | Duplicate title tag | 0.40 | 0.20 | auto |
| `h1_missing` | medium | No H1 heading | 0.40 | 0.10 | auto |
| `image_alt_missing` | medium | Image without alt text | 0.30 | 0.10 | auto |
| `meta_description_missing` | medium | Missing meta description | 0.35 | 0.10 | auto |
| `no_internal_links_out` | medium | Page links to nothing internally | 0.35 | 0.20 | auto |
| `duplicate_meta_description` | low | Duplicate meta description | 0.25 | 0.20 | auto |
| `h1_multiple` | low | More than one H1 | 0.20 | 0.20 | auto |
| `heading_hierarchy_broken` | low | Heading levels skip | 0.20 | 0.20 | auto |
| `title_too_long` | low | Title is longer than the search snippet | 0.25 | 0.10 | auto |
| `title_too_short` | low | Title is very short | 0.25 | 0.10 | auto |

**`duplicate_content`** — Duplicate page content

- *Why it matters:* Identical content splits signals between URLs and can suppress all of them.
- *What to do:* Consolidate to one URL and redirect or canonicalise the rest.

**`thin_content`** — Thin content

- *Why it matters:* Too little substance to satisfy the query or to be worth citing.
- *What to do:* Expand with specifics, or merge into a stronger page and redirect.

**`title_missing`** — Missing title tag

- *Why it matters:* The title is the strongest on-page relevance signal and the search result headline.
- *What to do:* Write a title of 50 to 60 characters that leads with the page's primary topic.

**`content_stale`** — Content has not been updated in over 18 months

- *Why it matters:* Freshness matters for queries where the answer changes, and stale pages decay.
- *What to do:* Refresh the facts, dates and examples, then update the modified date.

**`duplicate_title`** — Duplicate title tag

- *Why it matters:* Identical titles make pages compete and give searchers no reason to pick one.
- *What to do:* Write a distinct title reflecting each page's specific topic.

**`h1_missing`** — No H1 heading

- *Why it matters:* The H1 confirms the page topic to readers, assistive technology and crawlers.
- *What to do:* Add one H1 that matches the page's primary topic.

**`image_alt_missing`** — Image without alt text

- *Why it matters:* Alt text is an accessibility requirement and the only way image search understands the file.
- *What to do:* Describe the image in plain language, or use an empty alt if it is decorative.

**`meta_description_missing`** — Missing meta description

- *Why it matters:* Search engines will assemble a snippet themselves, usually less persuasively.
- *What to do:* Write 140 to 160 characters that state the benefit and invite the click.

**`no_internal_links_out`** — Page links to nothing internally

- *Why it matters:* A page that links nowhere is a dead end for both users and authority flow.
- *What to do:* Add contextual links to the most relevant related pages.

**`duplicate_meta_description`** — Duplicate meta description

- *Why it matters:* Repeated descriptions lower click-through because the snippet is not about this page.
- *What to do:* Write a distinct description for each page.

**`h1_multiple`** — More than one H1

- *Why it matters:* Multiple H1s blur which topic the page is actually about.
- *What to do:* Keep one H1 and demote the others to H2.

**`heading_hierarchy_broken`** — Heading levels skip

- *Why it matters:* Jumping from H2 to H4 breaks document outline for screen readers and parsers.
- *What to do:* Use heading levels in order without gaps.

**`title_too_long`** — Title is longer than the search snippet

- *Why it matters:* Truncated titles hide the part that would have earned the click.
- *What to do:* Trim to roughly 60 characters, keeping the distinguishing words first.

**`title_too_short`** — Title is very short

- *Why it matters:* A short title leaves relevance and click-through on the table.
- *What to do:* Expand it to describe what the page actually answers.

## ecommerce

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `faceted_nav_crawl_waste` | high | Faceted navigation is generating crawlable duplicate URLs | 0.60 | 0.50 | - |
| `product_schema_incomplete` | high | Product markup is missing merchant listing fields | 0.60 | 0.30 | auto |
| `out_of_stock_indexed` | medium | Out of stock products are indexed as live | 0.35 | 0.30 | - |

**`faceted_nav_crawl_waste`** — Faceted navigation is generating crawlable duplicate URLs

- *Why it matters:* Filter combinations can multiply into millions of near-identical pages.
- *What to do:* Canonicalise or block the combinations that have no search demand.

**`product_schema_incomplete`** — Product markup is missing merchant listing fields

- *Why it matters:* Without price, availability and identifiers the product cannot appear in shopping surfaces.
- *What to do:* Add offers, price, priceCurrency, availability and a GTIN or MPN.

**`out_of_stock_indexed`** — Out of stock products are indexed as live

- *Why it matters:* Sending searchers to something they cannot buy wastes the click and the trust.
- *What to do:* Keep the page, update availability in the markup and offer alternatives.

## international

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hreflang_missing_return` | high | Hreflang has no return tag | 0.50 | 0.30 | auto |
| `hreflang_invalid_code` | medium | Invalid hreflang language or region code | 0.35 | 0.20 | auto |
| `no_x_default` | low | No x-default hreflang | 0.20 | 0.20 | auto |

**`hreflang_missing_return`** — Hreflang has no return tag

- *Why it matters:* Hreflang is only honoured when every version points back at the others.
- *What to do:* Add reciprocal hreflang annotations on all versions.

**`hreflang_invalid_code`** — Invalid hreflang language or region code

- *Why it matters:* An invalid code is ignored, so the targeting silently does nothing.
- *What to do:* Use valid ISO 639-1 language and ISO 3166-1 Alpha 2 region codes.

**`no_x_default`** — No x-default hreflang

- *Why it matters:* Users outside your targeted regions get an arbitrary version.
- *What to do:* Add an x-default pointing at the language selector or the global version.

## local

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gbp_incomplete` | high | Google Business Profile is incomplete | 0.60 | 0.30 | auto |
| `nap_inconsistent` | high | Business name, address or phone is inconsistent | 0.60 | 0.40 | - |
| `gbp_no_recent_posts` | medium | No recent Google Business Profile posts | 0.35 | 0.20 | auto |
| `missing_location_page` | medium | No landing page for this location | 0.50 | 0.60 | - |
| `reviews_unanswered` | medium | Reviews have no response | 0.40 | 0.20 | auto |
| `citation_missing` | low | Missing directory citation | 0.25 | 0.30 | - |

**`gbp_incomplete`** — Google Business Profile is incomplete

- *Why it matters:* Profile completeness correlates directly with map pack visibility.
- *What to do:* Fill categories, services, hours, attributes and photos.

**`nap_inconsistent`** — Business name, address or phone is inconsistent

- *Why it matters:* Conflicting NAP data undermines the confidence that drives map pack ranking.
- *What to do:* Standardise one exact format and correct every listing to match.

**`gbp_no_recent_posts`** — No recent Google Business Profile posts

- *Why it matters:* An inactive profile signals an inactive business to both users and the ranking system.
- *What to do:* Post weekly: offers, updates, events.

**`missing_location_page`** — No landing page for this location

- *Why it matters:* Each location needs a page to rank for its own city and to link the profile to.
- *What to do:* Build a location page with unique local content, embedded map and LocalBusiness schema.

**`reviews_unanswered`** — Reviews have no response

- *Why it matters:* Responding is a documented local ranking factor and changes how prospects read the profile.
- *What to do:* Reply to every review, positive and negative.

**`citation_missing`** — Missing directory citation

- *Why it matters:* Citations on authoritative directories reinforce the entity and its NAP.
- *What to do:* Claim and complete the listing.

## offpage

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `toxic_backlinks` | high | Toxic backlinks detected | 0.50 | 0.40 | - |
| `authority_gap` | medium | Competitors have substantially more referring domains | 0.55 | 0.80 | - |
| `lost_backlinks` | medium | Backlinks lost | 0.40 | 0.40 | - |
| `unlinked_mention` | medium | Brand mentioned without a link | 0.40 | 0.20 | - |

**`toxic_backlinks`** — Toxic backlinks detected

- *Why it matters:* Links from spam networks can drag a site down and occasionally trigger a manual action.
- *What to do:* Verify before acting, then disavow only what is clearly manipulative.

**`authority_gap`** — Competitors have substantially more referring domains

- *Why it matters:* For competitive queries, link authority is often the binding constraint.
- *What to do:* Build a linkable asset and run targeted outreach.

**`lost_backlinks`** — Backlinks lost

- *Why it matters:* Losing earned links reverses the authority that earned the rankings.
- *What to do:* Check whether the page changed or was removed, then ask for reinstatement.

**`unlinked_mention`** — Brand mentioned without a link

- *Why it matters:* The hardest part, the coverage, already happened. The link is one email away.
- *What to do:* Ask the author to link the mention.

## performance

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inp_poor` | high | Interaction to Next Paint is poor | 0.55 | 0.70 | - |
| `lcp_poor` | high | Largest Contentful Paint is poor | 0.60 | 0.60 | - |
| `cls_poor` | medium | Cumulative Layout Shift is poor | 0.45 | 0.40 | - |
| `excessive_javascript` | medium | Very large JavaScript payload | 0.40 | 0.70 | - |
| `image_oversized` | medium | Oversized image | 0.40 | 0.30 | auto |
| `image_legacy_format` | low | Image uses a legacy format | 0.25 | 0.30 | auto |
| `image_no_dimensions` | low | Image has no width and height | 0.25 | 0.10 | auto |

**`inp_poor`** — Interaction to Next Paint is poor

- *Why it matters:* INP above 200ms makes the page feel broken when a user taps something.
- *What to do:* Break up long tasks and cut unused JavaScript on the critical path.

**`lcp_poor`** — Largest Contentful Paint is poor

- *Why it matters:* LCP above 2.5s is a Core Web Vitals failure and costs conversions directly.
- *What to do:* Optimise the hero element: preload it, compress it, remove render-blocking work above it.

**`cls_poor`** — Cumulative Layout Shift is poor

- *Why it matters:* Content jumping under a user's finger is the most complained-about page behaviour there is.
- *What to do:* Reserve space for images, ads and late-loading embeds.

**`excessive_javascript`** — Very large JavaScript payload

- *Why it matters:* Parse and execution time on mid-range phones is where most performance is lost.
- *What to do:* Code-split, defer what is not needed for first paint, drop unused libraries.

**`image_oversized`** — Oversized image

- *Why it matters:* Large images are the most common cause of a poor Largest Contentful Paint.
- *What to do:* Compress, resize to the displayed dimensions and serve WebP or AVIF.

**`image_legacy_format`** — Image uses a legacy format

- *Why it matters:* WebP and AVIF are typically 25 to 50 percent smaller at the same quality.
- *What to do:* Convert to WebP or AVIF with a fallback.

**`image_no_dimensions`** — Image has no width and height

- *Why it matters:* Missing dimensions cause layout shift as the image loads.
- *What to do:* Set explicit width and height attributes.

## schema

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schema_contradicts_page` | high | Structured data does not match the visible page | 0.70 | 0.30 | - |
| `schema_invalid` | high | Structured data is invalid | 0.50 | 0.30 | auto |
| `schema_missing` | medium | No structured data | 0.45 | 0.30 | auto |
| `schema_missing_required` | medium | Structured data is missing required properties | 0.40 | 0.20 | auto |

**`schema_contradicts_page`** — Structured data does not match the visible page

- *Why it matters:* Markup that describes content a user cannot see is a manual action risk.
- *What to do:* Make the markup describe exactly what is on the page.

**`schema_invalid`** — Structured data is invalid

- *Why it matters:* Invalid JSON-LD is ignored entirely, so the effort already spent earns nothing.
- *What to do:* Fix the syntax or the missing required properties.

**`schema_missing`** — No structured data

- *Why it matters:* Without schema the page cannot earn rich results and is harder for answer engines to parse.
- *What to do:* Add the JSON-LD type that matches this page: Article, Product, LocalBusiness, FAQPage.

**`schema_missing_required`** — Structured data is missing required properties

- *Why it matters:* Rich results need the required fields; without them the markup is decorative.
- *What to do:* Add the properties this type requires.

## technical

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `no_https` | critical | Page is not served over HTTPS | 0.90 | 0.50 | - |
| `page_5xx` | critical | Server error | 1.00 | 0.60 | - |
| `page_noindex` | critical | Page is blocked from indexing | 1.00 | 0.20 | - |
| `redirect_loop` | critical | Redirect loop | 1.00 | 0.40 | - |
| `robots_blocks_important` | critical | robots.txt blocks a page that should rank | 1.00 | 0.20 | - |
| `canonical_mismatch` | high | Canonical points to a different page | 0.70 | 0.20 | - |
| `mixed_content` | high | HTTPS page loads insecure resources | 0.50 | 0.30 | - |
| `no_sitemap` | high | No XML sitemap found | 0.60 | 0.30 | auto |
| `page_404_linked` | high | Broken internal link | 0.60 | 0.20 | auto |
| `canonical_missing` | medium | No canonical tag | 0.40 | 0.20 | auto |
| `orphan_page` | medium | Orphan page | 0.50 | 0.30 | auto |
| `redirect_chain` | medium | Redirect chain | 0.40 | 0.30 | auto |
| `sitemap_contains_non_indexable` | medium | Sitemap lists pages that cannot be indexed | 0.40 | 0.20 | auto |
| `deep_page` | low | Page is more than four clicks from the homepage | 0.30 | 0.30 | auto |

**`no_https`** — Page is not served over HTTPS

- *Why it matters:* HTTPS is a ranking signal and browsers warn users on insecure pages.
- *What to do:* Install a certificate and redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS.

**`page_5xx`** — Server error

- *Why it matters:* A 5xx page cannot be indexed and burns crawl budget on every visit.
- *What to do:* Fix the server error. If the page is retired, return 410 or redirect it.

**`page_noindex`** — Page is blocked from indexing

- *Why it matters:* A noindex directive removes the page from search results entirely.
- *What to do:* Remove the noindex meta tag or X-Robots-Tag header if this page should rank.

**`redirect_loop`** — Redirect loop

- *Why it matters:* The URL never resolves, so neither users nor crawlers reach content.
- *What to do:* Break the loop and point the chain at a single final URL.

**`robots_blocks_important`** — robots.txt blocks a page that should rank

- *Why it matters:* Disallowed URLs cannot be crawled, so their content never enters the index.
- *What to do:* Narrow the Disallow rule so it no longer covers this path.

**`canonical_mismatch`** — Canonical points to a different page

- *Why it matters:* The page is telling search engines to index something else, so it will not rank.
- *What to do:* Point the canonical at this URL unless it really is a duplicate.

**`mixed_content`** — HTTPS page loads insecure resources

- *Why it matters:* Browsers block or warn on mixed content, breaking the page for some users.
- *What to do:* Serve every subresource over HTTPS.

**`no_sitemap`** — No XML sitemap found

- *Why it matters:* A sitemap is how a search engine learns about pages your internal links miss.
- *What to do:* Publish an XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt.

**`page_404_linked`** — Broken internal link

- *Why it matters:* Internal links to 404s waste crawl budget and strand users mid-journey.
- *What to do:* Repoint the link to the live URL or remove it.

**`canonical_missing`** — No canonical tag

- *Why it matters:* Without a canonical, parameter and variant URLs compete with each other.
- *What to do:* Add a self-referencing canonical to every indexable page.

**`orphan_page`** — Orphan page

- *Why it matters:* No internal link points here, so it gets little crawl attention and no internal authority.
- *What to do:* Link to it from a relevant hub or category page.

**`redirect_chain`** — Redirect chain

- *Why it matters:* Each extra hop loses a little authority and adds latency.
- *What to do:* Point the first URL straight at the final destination.

**`sitemap_contains_non_indexable`** — Sitemap lists pages that cannot be indexed

- *Why it matters:* Submitting noindex or redirected URLs sends a contradictory signal.
- *What to do:* Remove non-indexable URLs from the sitemap.

**`deep_page`** — Page is more than four clicks from the homepage

- *Why it matters:* Depth correlates with crawl frequency and with how much internal authority a page receives.
- *What to do:* Add a link from a shallower hub page.

## ux

| Code | Severity | Check | Impact | Effort | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `intent_mismatch` | high | Page format does not match search intent | 0.70 | 0.60 | - |
| `mobile_unfriendly` | high | Page is not mobile friendly | 0.70 | 0.50 | - |
| `no_clear_cta` | medium | No clear call to action | 0.50 | 0.30 | - |

**`intent_mismatch`** — Page format does not match search intent

- *Why it matters:* A product page cannot win an informational query however well it is optimised.
- *What to do:* Match the format the ranking results use, or target a different query.

**`mobile_unfriendly`** — Page is not mobile friendly

- *Why it matters:* Indexing is mobile-first, and most traffic is mobile.
- *What to do:* Fix the viewport, tap targets and horizontal overflow.

**`no_clear_cta`** — No clear call to action

- *Why it matters:* Traffic that cannot convert is a cost, not a result.
- *What to do:* Add one primary action above the fold that matches the page's intent.
